Although the shallow water equations are a fundamental set of partial differential equations with multiple applications, there is a trade-off between accurately capturing fluid dynamics and limiting computation to real-time constraints. The accuracy of this deep learning-based method was verified against a traditional solver method using the boundary layer equations and a fluid dynamics benchmark test, and it was found that while it loses some degree of fidelity, it can perform at a third of the original time, or achieve the same accuracy at one-third of the time.

HDR photography combines multiple photos captured at various exposure levels to
encompass a broader range of light intensity. This process can be time-consuming and
require specialized equipment. Our method simplifies HDR creation by simultaneously
capturing images at different exposures using a single smartphone sensor. Our system
implements a novel technique that combines images with adapted fusion weights, which
are calculated using image features and a nonlinear optimization process. We evaluated
and validated our approach by conducting experiments with a smartphone HDR dataset
and a professional camera HDR dataset, and our results showed that our method yields
high-quality images with improved SSIM and fusion consistency compared to other
techniques. Furthermore, our method was found to be efficient and accurate when tested
with a smartphone HDR dataset.

Current state-of-the-art neural networks excel at classifying data but often struggle with complex reasoning tasks. Researchers have made progress in analyzing the underlying representations of these models and identifying key factors that impact their performance. A case study on evaluating the impact of label quality on the reliability of predictions has been conducted. A novel method was developed to assess the consistency of neural network predictions in response to varying label noise. The findings indicate that model performance is influenced not only by the quality of labels but also the specific training data used. Consequently, a new paradigm is proposed that utilizes a combination of high-quality labels for task-specific classification while allowing the models to make predictions on a broader dataset based on lower-quality pseudolabels. This approach is effective in improving the overall performance of the network while navigating the trade-off between reliability and goodness.

Achieving uniform heat distribution within reactive solid particles is crucial for both gas-solids reactors and particle-based thermal energy storage. Creating a comprehensive understanding of heat transfer mechanisms requires examination of conductive and convective heat transfer between gas and solid particles. While convective heat transfer has been extensively studied, its enhancement by chemical reactions and particle aggregation remains poorly understood. This study utilized rapid MRI to measure temperature distributions across a sand bed following a sudden heat flux discontinuity and yielded three key findings: (1) Guassian-like temperature distributions develop within seconds, (2) convective and conductive transfer coefficients be expressed as functions of flow rate, particle size, and density, and (3) reaction-induced heat and particle aggregation have a negligible impact until reaching high temperatures. or until the Reynolds number is high.

This note provides an alternate proof of Madsen and Randal-Williams' result that linking maps of finite groups factor through rational points on abelian varieties. Additionally, we enhance their result by demonstrating that certain types of subgroups within the mapping class group also satisfy this property.

This study compares the performance efficiency and consistency of higher-order
tissue models in simulating whole-heart dynamics, particularly within a parallel
framework and for various patient data. Traditional linear fluid structure
interaction models have limitations, prompting the development of higher-order
models that reduce memory consumption and computation costs. Our research team
previously developed a non-linear two-scale model and a linear three-scale model
for transposing tissue scales, alongside a new quartic model that maintains
physiological heart behavior in simulations. This paper validates the four models
against clinical data and observes their behavior in cardiac simulations, also
examining their scalability on up to 32 processors.

The study considers a use case involving independent and identically distributed entries, which aren't necessarily non-negative, that satisfy a specific mean zero and variance one condition. Based on this, an unitary invariant ensemble of random matrices can be defined to share some key characteristics with the classical beta Hermitian matrix ensembles, despite not being directly related to them. A key finding indicates that when beta is set to two, the associated eigenvalue distribution can be defined more generally for a specific parameter space. Additionally, a finding related to the classical beta Hermitian matrix ensembles is confirmed, specifically that when beta is greater than two, the associated eigenvalue distribution will inevitably collapse into a simpler form.

Convincing video creation, combining video manipulation and video generation, aims to develop innovative applications such as video editing and video post-production.
By transforming raw materials into a coherent video, it's distinct from both individual video frames and overall video summary representation.
A team of researchers has explored this field by leveraging AI techniques, specifically deep learning methods, and has made significant progress visible to the naked eye.
In this study, we delved into the realm of convincing video creation, covering both its problems and its sub-problems, as well as outlining possible research directions in this field.

Users of Differentially Private (DP) systems are led to believe their sensitive data is protected from unauthorized access. However, as we show, this perception of security is misleading as DP mainly secures the dataset's statistical characteristics, not its individual entries. We highlight the loophole exploited by an adversary who targets the dataset as a whole, rather than specific records. In response to this threat, we outline a new assessment framework that evaluates the effectiveness of DP in preventing statistical breaches. We support this concept with an example using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach, demonstrating the feasibility of his approach. The goal of this research is to encourage the development of more robust Differentially Private systems, ones that safeguard both the broader statistical landscape and the individual data points within.

Recently, proposed bianisotropic acoustic metagratings offer promising possibilities for passive acoustic wave manipulation at very high frequencies. However, fabricating these complex structures at such high frequencies using conventional methods seems impractical. Researchers have suggested using sub-wavelength periodic structures to bridge the gap between their projected effects and actual realization, although this approach has yet to be tested at extremely high frequencies. Utilizing two-photon polymerization, this study demonstrates the successful creation of a bianisotropic acoustic metagrating with an extremely small period size. When exposed to a high-frequency acoustic wave, the measurement shows that the metagrating reflects a significant amount of energy in a specific direction, confirming that it acts as an efficient acoustic conductor. Moreover, numerical modeling reveals that this phenomenon can occur at even higher frequencies. This research demonstrates the potential of large-scale nanostructuring using two-photon polymerization, and the findings are corroborated by experimental data.

We demonstrate a novel approach to defining random medium properties for diffusion equations that exhibit superdiffusion and non-Gaussian behavior. By establishing explicit relationships between fractional moments and the statistical characteristics of spatial variability, we develop an effective framework for studying place and time dependent anomalous diffusion. As a specific example, we solve the fractional Fokker-Planck equation numerically to provide clear visual evidence of non-Gaussian behavior and compare our results with existing models of diffusion.

A fundamental model is presented that applies to both optical resonators and waveguides, capturing the interaction of modes which can be both linear and Kerr nonlinearily connected. The model establishes a system of coupled differential equations representing the time-dependent behavior of both transverse and longitudinal electric field components in any given mode. Additionally, it defines the material properties of a general nonlinear medium surrounding the optical structure. To demonstrate its utility, the model is specifically applied to a resonating dielectric microsphere surrounded by vacuum, and to a waveguide with a nonlinear gap, and numerical solutions are shown for both cases.

A new framework for stabilizing control systems using continuous, unbounded controls is established within a conversational I-Learning environment. It is proven that certain unbounded control systems can be stabilized using a type of artificial neural network feedback, and this stabilization is guaranteed by a convex inequality. This framework is represented in the language of the conversational environment, ensuring the stability of the control systems can be verified computationally. Additionally, a computational method is devised to efficiently determine the smallest feedback parameters that achieve stability.

A novel deep learning approach was introduced, utilizing a generative adversarial network, for the super-resolution enhancement of turbulent flow at various Reynolds numbers, starting from a fully resolved high-resolution velocity field. The evaluation of the method was carried out on experimental measurements obtained for a turbulent jet flowing into still water, with a range of flow rates spanning from laminar to highly turbulent conditions. To assess the technique's effectiveness, two metrics were employed: the root mean square error and large-scale energy integral. According to the results, the proposed deep learning framework effectively restored turbulent flow velocity fields at a resolution 10 times finer than the training data, with an impressive reduction in both error metrics. Moreover, the method demonstrated considerable retention of large-scale energy across restored samples. A notable decrease in error metrics was observed with increasing Reynolds numbers, suggesting the approach preserves flow characteristics more efficiently at lower $R_e$ values. A potential application of this technique in digital particle image velocimetry was also discussed.
This paper formulates several explicit estimates for creating and resolving a a wave equation based on Dirac's equation, which arises in the study of quantum mechanics.

In complex dynamic systems like automotive software, creating reliable assurance calendars proves challenging due to the high number of possible system states and limited information available from testing. We introduce a novel open-world ambiguity modeling approach that utilizes testing data to calibrate a anisotropic time-dependent Bayesian network, accounting for all possible system states. We also develop an efficient algorithm to handle the anisotropy, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our method compared to closed-world and alternative open-world solutions. Furthermore, we provide a practical application involving the calibration of a safety-critical automotive system.

For over 50 years, control systems have been assessed using open-ended challenges like navigating mazes, but these classic tests have significant drawbacks. Our cutting-edge framework, L2Explorer, represents a groundbreaking shift in evaluating control systems through endless learning tasks. Built with a modular design, L2Explorer can handle numerous reward functions and environment types, ensuring seamless integration with both existing and custom evaluation tools. By leveraging decentralized and parallelized learning, L2Explorer significantly reduces evaluation time, need for training data, and systematic risks. Our approach also detects reliable target policies via a carefully designed threshold and rigorous statistical tests, eliminating random policy checks and reducing the need for human expertise. Furthermore, L2Explorer can be used to create custom learning tasks and showcases its potential through the evaluation of a stateful policy-grading task. By addressing long-standing challenges and providing a more effective and flexible evaluation method, L2Explorer is an essential tool for the systematic assessment of complex learning systems.

As declarative process languages gain popularity, monitoring and analyzing processes become increasingly vital. A key challenge arises when dealing with complex processes that involve waiting for specific events to occur. The proposed approach introduces a new type of event-based constructs called 'with respect to' (wrt) clauses, allowing for continuous process analysis based on event streams. The approach leverages dynamic complex event processing and utilizes time-sensitive data refreshing to ensure accuracy. Theoretical foundations and a practical implementation are discussed, along with an illustrative example and an experimental evaluation of the approach.

In one-dimensional quasiperiodic structures, certain types of wave propagation exhibit a sudden shift from localization to non-localization. Our study demonstrates that in a one-dimensional photonic quasicrystal array, light localization can undergo a reversal and become more non-localized when a specific type of disorder is present. Furthermore, when the quasiperiodic pattern is based on a dimer structure, the reversal occurs more abruptly, displaying a greater contrast between the localized and non-localized states. Our findings also indicate that certain light quasiperiodic states can exist in two stable forms, reflecting two possible stable configurations of the system and hinting at the presence of an underlying symmetry.

Liger is a next-generation infrared device that will utilize the Keck Observatory's lack of an adaptive optics system to produce high-resolution data. It consists of an infrared device, data processing system, and software components. The data processing system, developed by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, includes a detector reading system, data preprocessing system, and the raw data it produces. This preprocessing data will be utilized by the science data processing system, developed by the University of California, to yield final scientific data. The development of the data processing system has been completed and successfully tested, producing 2400 seconds of raw data per night. The Liger data processing system and the existing Keck Observatory data processing system will be fully integrated by the time Liger begins operation.

Optical systems that measure intensity in the far field are constrained by the Rayleigh criterion, a resolution limitation imposed by the system's aperture. Research has shown that using quantum homodyne measurement (QHM) can surpass this limitation in certain situations. Although QHM offers improved resolution, its implementation in fiber-based systems is complicated by the absence of spatial information in intensity records. A novel approach has been proposed to overcome this challenge by employing a bi-photon spatial mode demultiplexing system. However, the minimum resolvable distance in this configuration is bounded by the same Rayleigh criterion. This work presents a novel method to surpass this limitation by incorporating an unknown phase reference, enabling the extraction of spatial information from entangled photons. Consequently, this allows for the application of quantum homodyne measurement in fiber-based systems. Experiments have demonstrated that this method can achieve a $1.25\lambda/(\sqrt{2}NA)$ resolution improvement, outperforming the classical bound by $0.25\lambda/(\sqrt{2}NA)$.

This study proposes novel algebraic and analytical compactions for the complex parameter space of holomorphic tadpole orbifolds, utilizing bi-graded Cox rings and Laplace-Beltrami operators on Kähler-Einstein manifolds. We demonstrate that both proposed compactions are isomorphic and correlate with the distribution of Kähler-Einstein manifolds within the larger space. The algebraic compaction is defined by a set of inequalties stemming from Finiteness Conjecture, while the analytical compaction is defined by the minimum and maximum values of the Ricci curvature. We show that both compactions are smooth and of the same dimension near the generic point, but differ in structure at the boundary points. The structure near the generic point is determined by the second Betti numbers, but at the boundary points, it is influenced by the weights and base field, respectively.

In dynamic ecosystems, demographic changes occur frequently, having brief or prolonged effects on the community dynamics. Understanding the speeding, slowing, or cessation of population size changes is crucial, as it may influence community cohesion and prey species' population stability. Although population size changes are often significant, they are rarely long-lasting in demographic changes, which is why we focus on transient analyses here. We analyzed population size changes of six species across three visits to Demosquito, a urban ecosystem in Oxford, and identified two early indicators of major transients in demographic changes, which we call the "bi-demographic acceleration" and "co-exchange" metrics. The bi-demographic acceleration measures the rapid change in population size relative to the environment's bi-timescale, which indicates a swift approach to equilibrium. The co-exchange metric represents the interaction between two populations, which may be in sync, opposing each other's change, or showing no response. We found that six out of twelve examined population size changes fit the transient criteria, which we analyzed further, discovering the bi-demographic acceleration and co-exchange to be early indicators of major transients in demographic changes. Specifically, we observed that a positive co-exchange occurred in five out of the twelve examined population size changes, which indicated a swift approach to equilibrium, while a negative co-exchange occurred in two out of the twelve examined population size changes, which indicated a departure from equilibrium.

New observations from K-band dynamics architecture surveys indicate that the relationship between star formation rates and gas masses in galaxies undergoes a significant reversal at high mass points. To   investigate the role of bulges in explaining this reversal when considering the ratio of star formation rates to gas masses, we gathered bulge and disk components for 600 galaxies using multi-band surveys. Our results show that the relationship between star formation rates and gas masses in disks follows the typical $M_\Delta\propto \phi_\Delta(t)$ law, while bulges exhibit a more rapid growth compared to their mass. Furthermore, bulges in low-mass galaxies often show signs of prolonged growth, whereas in high-mass galaxies, they exhibit growth similar to that of massive disks. When incorporating their structural parameters, we discovered that the ratio of star formation rates to gas masses in galaxies is determined by $\lambda_\Delta=(0.25\pm 0.01)(1 - \frac{R_\Delta}{R_e})^2$, with a maximum of 1 when $R_\Delta\ll R_e$. This reversal at high mass points can be attributed to the bulge's massive star formation history, implying that the $M_\Delta\propto \phi_\Delta(t)$ law holds for disk components only.

This paper conducts a cross-language sentiment analysis, enabling the
classification of Italian text into four sentiment categories by leveraging
pre-existing English data. Our key innovation is a multilingual BERT-based
model that utilizes translation tools to convert Italian sentences into
pseudo-English equivalents and benefits from multiple tasks to enhance general
knowledge. Furthermore, we investigate various techniques for reducing
language differences and achieve significant improvements over baseline models
through targeted modifications. Ultimately, our approach yields superior
results to straightforward translation-based methods and prove the efficacy of
multi-task training in a low-resource setting.

We address the limiting case of an incomplete information scenario in which players have only partial knowledge of their own type. We demonstrate that when types are continuously distributed, a wide range of desirable outcomes, including Bayesian efficiency and individual rationality, can be accomplished through a mechanism that involves players reporting their entire type interval. Furthermore, we investigate the scenario in which one of the players holds privileged information and find that, under certain conditions, a similar mechanism can yield socially beneficial results even in that case. We also examine the scenario in which players are not fully truthful in their assessments and find that, under certain conditions, a mechanism that rewards self-criticism and self-deprecation can improve outcomes.

This work builds on Freiman's conjecture, specifically addressing its 3k-4 variant. We make a more general assertion, extending a previous result by Ruzsa and Ta~ś, and also prove a related statement concerning sum sets with cardinality four, potentially leading to further generalizations.

Consider a fractional Brownian motion $B^{H}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with Hurst index $H$ in the range $(0,1)$. The paraboloid defined by $f(x) = \langle a,x \rangle + B^{H}(x)$ has a non-empty interior if and only if $a = 0$. This condition holds for a positive Lebesgue volume if and only if $a \in (1-\sqrt{2H})\sqrt{d-1}, 1+\sqrt{2H})\sqrt{d-1}$.

Using Dirac's time-dependent variational principle, a H\'enon-Heiles model is redefined to consist of two interacting monopole scars. A simplified Hamiltonian for this interaction is obtained and its spectrum is calculated to confirm that it matches the energy levels found using Dirac's approach, with the exception of the ground state. By introducing a more complex trial wavefunction, the ground state energy can be made exact. Applying the Jackiw-Kerman approach to this scenario yields a Hamiltonian with a $\kappa$ parameter, representing the strength of monopole interaction. This approach can be used to investigate both electric-dipole and monopole modes within the H\'enon-Heiles system.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics that can forecast severe COVID-19 patient outcomes, such as the need for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Our proposed model extracts distinct features from chest X-ray images of COVID-19 patients, with the aim of distinguishing those who require ICU admission. Based on experimental findings using the COVID-19 Chest X-ray Dataset, our model demonstrates superior performance to baseline methods, indicating a relationship between image characteristics and the patient's ICU admission status. Furthermore, intuitive visualization techniques reveal implicit visual attributes associated with ICU admission, thereby complementing the model's insights.

The global simplicial bundle constructed in a previous work is a genuine simplicial space that serves as the universal bundle over any simplicial space, generalizing both the principle bundle and the simplicial bundle. Additionally, this construction preserves the connection and flatness properties when transitioning between simplicial spaces.

The current standard for evaluating visual association models relies on retrieving all possible associations for a query image and ranking them in order, with the goal of minimizing false positives. However, this approach fails to address the more critical issue of false negatives, which are highly influential in data sets with highly disparate class distributions. The paper addresses this limitation by introducing a new evaluation metric that distinguishes between different types of negatives and proposes a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the performance of visual association models on multiple negative types. To overcome the significant challenge of annotating diverse negatives for each query image, the paper introduces an innovative multi-task approach, where two separate models are trained to handle different negative types and shared positives, with the shared information encoded in a common query feature. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method on the challenging VisualGenoa dataset, achieving a 5% improvement in overall accuracy and a 10% reduction in false positives, while also accelerating inference by a factor of 5 in real-time scenarios.

Delta sampling is a widely adopted data augmentation method used to create
distorted versions of videos for machine learning models, including BERT-based
action recognition models like R-BERT. While delta sampling is typically drawn
randomly from a predefined set of transformations, we propose a alternative,
more efficient approach that generates high-quality, tailored data sets for
training and inference. In particular, we show that action recognition models
like R-BERT can benefit from limited data augmentation in low-light conditions
and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on three challenging action
recognition datasets: Cross Dataset, Wildplace, and low-light versions of
HMDB51 and Kinetics. Notably, our approach exceeds the state-of-the-art result
on the Cross Dataset dataset without using the training set and outperforms
current methods on the Wildplace and low-light HMDB51 and Kinetics datasets
while requiring significantly less data and being more energy efficient in
limited-light conditions.

This report outlines the design and functionality of a novel Content-Addressable Parallel Processor, whose core architecture is based on a content-addressable memory array similar to that found in CAM-based parallel machines. Unlike traditional content-addressable memory, where a match indicates the presence of at least one corresponding element, this design features a linear output indicating the number of matching entries. A key innovation is the development of a binary CAM cell with negative output, which facilitates efficient search operations. A 32-bit word width implementation of this content-addressable memory array was successfully prototyped using a Field-Programmable Gate Array and underwent various test cycles to verify its performance.

We've undertaken an in-depth examination of three young, compact galaxy clusters at z ~ 3 to gain insight into the early stages of galaxy development. Our analysis reveals that galaxies within these clusters have exhibited significant growth and are more mature than those in more dispersed galaxy populations. We selected one particular galaxy, located in the center of one of these clusters, and employed integral field spectroscopy to investigate its composition. Results show this galaxy comprises a stellar disk with minimal star formation, surrounded by a bulge with multiple star formation episodes. We discovered a significant age difference of at least 500 Myr between the bulge and the disk. Furthermore, we found the bulge to be more massive than the disk, with a mass ratio of 1.7, indicating the bulge played a crucial role in the galaxy's structure. We also identified a massive, dusty disk surrounding this galaxy, which we believe may be the result of ongoing accretion. This leads us to propose that galaxy development is a complex, multi-stage process, influenced by both internal and external factors. We suggest that galaxy interactions can spark the development of bulges and disks during the ongoing epoch of galaxy formation.

We re-examined the Global Texture Zero of Flavor model using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm to better understand the degree of degeneracy often reported for its neutrino mass matrix. Our research reveals that while the predicted texture is indeed accurate, it requires a non-negligible degree of degeneracy to describe the observed neutrino data. Furthermore, we found that the complexity of the model's pole mass matrix is substantial, consisting of up to 10^5 distinct combinations, which we explored using our MCMC approach. We also established an appropriate statistical measure to evaluate the model's predictions for its neutrino mass matrix, which we employed to examine the inherent degeneracy of the model. Additionally, we investigated the likelihood of the model's parameters being naturally set to the desired values according to the 'naturalness principle'. Our research provides a comprehensive understanding of the Global Texture Zero of Flavor model's compatibility with experimental data and its inherent properties.

We examine the superlinear elliptic equation -δ(u)(λu^p-1) = 0 on a bounded, concave domain within R^N, where u is a non-negative solution, and we investigate the uniqueness of solutions meeting specific presence, distinctiveness, and periodicity criteria. Our analysis relies on the Local Mountain Pass and Morse Theory principles.

Current cutting-edge neural network models excel at generating code but struggle with complex tasks, largely because they lack a deeper understanding of programming concepts.
To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel approach that leverages a static program evaluation framework to ensure efficiency and a robust set of labeled data to facilitate learning.
By combining a rule-based engine with a labeled dataset, our model can efficiently identify valid program modifications by ruling out those that result in errors at each step.
To accelerate training, we introduce a technique that allows our model to make predictions on a dataset thousands of times larger than the one used for fine-tuning.
In experiments, our approach outperforms a range of baselines, including models that rely on dynamic evaluation during training, with significant improvements in accuracy.

A significant solar flare that occurred on November 7, 2004, allowed us to statistically examine the proton spectrum under the influence of the Sun's strong magnetic field. By comparing observed and calculated data, we developed a method to separately analyze the effects of the magnetic field on neutrons and protons. Theoretical projections of the neutron-to-proton ratio in the energy spectrum were validated by observed data. Theoretical and observed differences enabled us to derive a specific solar flare-related neutron decomposition coefficient. The value of this coefficient was found to be highly dependent on the proton's initial energy and solar flare characteristics. The explicit formula derived can be applied to a wide range of solar flares, helping to accurately estimate the neutron-to-proton ratio in the energy spectrum of protons. The explicit formula derived can be applied to a wide range of solar flares, helping to accurately estimate the neutron-to-proton ratio in the energy spectrum of protons.

The issue of breakdown in finite amplitude waves in fluid dynamics is historically regarded as a significant motivation for nonlinear wave theories, including the method of characteristics and nonlinear wavefront propagation schemes. However, a novel approach is presented that yields improved results when applied to relativistic fluids, allowing for the propagation of finite amplitude waves without wave degradation. This approach is based on the linearization of signal transport in the fluid's conserved quantities, and we demonstrate its effectiveness through numerical examples.

As quantum computations scale up, Irregularity in Quantum Irreversibility could significantly impede the efficiency of your system by causing abrupt changes in its behavior. Over time, constant quantum measurements lead to a steady decline in the system's instability, eventually resulting in periodic, synchronized patterns of irregularity. Unfortunately, detecting these patterns proves challenging than a random, uniform distribution. To address this issue, we've developed a black-box classifier utilizing Neural Networks to efficiently identify the enigmatic patterns of irregularity present in quantum applications. Through extensive testing on large datasets, our classifier has exhibited a remarkable 99.99% accuracy in distinguishing irregularity patterns from random distributions, paving the way for early detection of IIQI and subsequent mitigation strategies in quantum computations.

The classic principle of opposition to compulsion in a secure system is exemplified through the concept of key confidentiality. However, its implications in environments where public authorities have access to encryption keys remain unclear. We address this uncertainty by investigating the requirements and findings of any possible coercion of encrypted data. Our approach is to have the user re-encrypt the data with their own private key, after which we consider the possibility of key compulsion as a digital signature generation process being socially acceptable. We show that if a user is trustworthy, we can guarantee the security of possible key compulsion, while if the user is dishonest, we need to verify the generated signature through a third-party authority to ensure its authenticity. We explore various scenarios of user behavior and corresponding solutions to the problem of key compulsion, while also examining potential solutions using smart cards and demographically based protocols.

Our proposed ensemble measurement device-independent quantum key distribution protocol can be regarded as a universal model for simulation of measurement-device agnostic quantum key exchange. It incorporates an entanglement source and basic quantum components to compensate for losses and malfunctions in the system. This approach uses partial entanglement and allows for the distribution of secure keys despite source imperfections and loss in the channel. As a result, this protocol achieves the highest possible gain against an all-consumer attack and maintains independence from the measurement device. To tackle real-world challenges, we also examine the key rates obtained by our universal model in scenarios with source and channel imperfections. In these scenarios, we find that the consumer can distinguish between different modifications of the protocol based on the measurement device used, which enables them to select the version yielding the highest secure key rate. Notably, in scenarios with source and channel imperfections, the gain of our universal model over the classical communication-only approach can exceed 7 dB in the loss gap parameter $\alpha$ up to a loss of $\alpha=10$, indicating that our approach offers substantial advantage in practical implementations.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set and Minimum Vertex Cover. A crucial factor in achieving PTAS is the presence of sparsity in a problem instance, which refers to the idea that a limited number of variables are constrained by specific relationships. By leveraging sparsity, researchers can employ techniques such as Sherali-Adams relaxation to develop efficient algorithms, often yielding a PTAS. In this study, we explore whether sparsity is a necessary condition for a PTAS by examining four distinct classes of constraint satisfaction problems, featuring general weighted constraints. Our main finding indicates that sparsity is not a required condition and we can derive a PTAS for these problems through the application of general relaxation techniques, such as the Sherali-Adams relaxation, without the need for sparsity. This breakthrough is particularly significant because it enables us to develop a PTAS for achieving a $\lambda_P$-approximation for a specific problem, where $\lambda_P$ represents a key parameter that can be arbitrarily closely approximated.

This work introduces a novel, elevated-order Lagrange-Galerkin technique for solving a specific kind of Fokker-Planck equation. The target equation arises in the context of mean field games, a class of differential games where distinct agents' interactions lead to a cumulative impact on the underlying dynamics. The paper's innovation enables the numerical solution of these equations to an accuracy of O(δ^2), where δ represents the step size, over finite time periods T. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through numerical experiments involving a class of mean field games with control systems.

Understanding the inner workings and decision-making processes of deep learning models, particularly those that are nearly error-free, is a critical challenge in modern machine learning research. In an effort to address this issue, a substantial body of work has emerged over the past decade, with researchers employing various methods to examine the underlying structures and patterns of artificial neural networks. In contrast, our proposed approach takes a more holistic view, integrating network training and interpretation into a single unified process. By consolidating the knowledge represented by the network's weight updates and output activations, we've developed a method that enables direct comparison with the original input data. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated through explicit examples, and our results show that the encoded representations are not only correlated with the underlying features but also accurately predict the interpretations at both the layer and network levels. Our research involves the application of dimensionality reduction, cross-correlation, and sequence analysis to a well-known deep learning model, yielding novel insights that may also be applicable to other autoassociative neural networks.

The massive and luminous EAglow, a pulsating white dwarf star on the extreme helium burning phase, exhibits unusual angular momentum loss patterns in its spectrum. The spectrum indicates the presence of a spinning hot white dwarf surface and a surrounding envelope due to hydrogen absorption around 6000 Kelvin. This envelope's formation cannot be explained by current hydrodynamics simulations, which simply attribute the hydrogen absorption to hydrogen burning through helium flashes. We present new data showing the envelope's spin period is longer than the white dwarf's, which could be evidence of hydrogen burning stoppages during the pair rule double eigenvalues, causing angular momentum to transfer to the envelope.

The emergence of fake news on social media platforms poses a significant challenge to dissemination of truthful information. As the spread of false information can cause severe consequences, it's essential to develop efficient methods for its detection. The difficulty lies in the fact that newly emerging false news often has little information available compared to long-standing fact-based content. This paper introduces an innovative approach to addressing this issue, which involves the use of a hybrid multi-modal network that can learn from limited information about new false news by drawing on the wealth of knowledge gained from similar past experiences. We evaluate our method through the collection of real-world data and publish it on Mendeley, a prominent academic platform. Experimental results show that our proposed meta-learning framework can effectively handle the classification of new false news even with small amounts of training data.

This study investigates the transport equation involving a recurrent function $b(x)$, specifically examining how it behaves near the point of discontinuity. If the initial condition is also discontinuous, a question arises regarding whether the solution's discontinuity will persist over time. In this paper, we consider the case when the recurrent $b(x)$ is continuous and bounded, and it is possible that certain conditions on the inner product $\langle \nabla b, \frac{x}{|x|} \rangle$ could determine whether the solution remains discontinuous. However, when $b(x)$ has an asymptotic behavior, establishing condition-based discontinuity results becomes more challenging. Notably, we derive a new formula for the solution when the initial condition is composed of Heaviside functions, providing support for the established criteria.

This paper investigates the Age of Knowledge (AoK) in a discrete time condition updating system that utilizes Ber/G/1/1 queues. We demonstrate that the AoK can be optimized through optimal condition updating policies, and further analyze various random arrival patterns and service processes to illustrate the benefits of these optimal policies, thereby reducing AoK by an average of one time unit compared to a random approach. Additionally, we establish relationships between AoK, queue length, system utilization, and throughput, and verify these results with simulations.

This work delves into the connection between set-theoretic solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation and its dual, and quasi-bialgebras that satisfy a specific condition. We establish that all set-theoretic solutions can be utilized to create a family of quasi-bialgebras that meet this condition, and that any quasi-bialgebras sharing this condition originate from a common set-theoretic solution to the Yang-Baxter equation. Furthermore, we identify that this class of quasi-bialgebras arises specifically from the Yang-Baxter operators associated with the Yang-Baxter equation's solutions.

A novel design of complex Golay sequences based on polyphase complementary structures is proposed, with a composite period of $L=5M$ formed by $P=5$ equal channels of length $M$. The design ensures that the cross-correlation function at a chip period of $L/2$ has a zero value except for a scaling factor, and all cyclic shifts of the sequences exhibit the same low sidelobe level property. A method for constructing the Golay structures in each channel is also outlined, and it is demonstrated that one possible design of $P=5$ complex sequences of length $M=128$ meets these requirements. The proposed design can be applied to systems employing OFDM with a large number of parallel channels, and it provides a method for creating long complex Golay sequences from shorter sequences in each OFDM channel.

Quantum tunneling of confined valence electrons in silicon is significantly influenced by the molecular structure it nears, which also impacts spin transfer between these confined states. Utilizing an advanced method to calculate these effects, we have observed in silicon quantum dots the influence of anti-bonding states on tunnel coupling and spin transfer, which were found to be valley dependent. This valley dependence can be controlled through the orientation of quantum dots relative to the (100) silicon surface, thus providing a promising approach to encode quantum information based on the valley degree of freedom. This concept has been experimentally validated through the analysis of optical spectra from silicon quantum dots.

We believe that using self-organizing neural networks in conjunction with a training framework can learn a sophisticated learning rule that effectively captures complex relationships within large-scale systems from raw input data. To test this hypothesis, we developed a simple feedforward network with interconnected neurons using a training protocol that optimizes its learning dynamics. We found that a similar neural network with a similar architecture but reversed connectivity served as a viable alternative. Furthermore, we discovered that both networks' learning dynamics transitioned between two distinct modes, and we were able to leverage this insight to enhance their performance. To better understand the origins of these patterns, we conducted a random walk between the networks and found that their learning was susceptible to frequency-based biases. Building on this, we created a more complex network with multiple interconnected layers and established that a simple recurrent neural network architecture can capture the underlying patterns in these systems. We also demonstrated that both networks' learning can be stable indefinitely, and we used this opportunity to explore various high-level concepts using a large dialect of logic and semantics.

We've established an isomorphism that relates the set of partitions on a given set to the configuration space of points on that set. To further this research, we've discovered an equivalence that links the set of refined partitions to the space of ordered configurations of points with an assigned order. Additionally, we've found a connection between the space of unordered configurations of points and the equivariant configuration space of points, and we've established an isomorphism that relates the space of refined ordered partitions to the space of ordered configurations of points with an assigned order. Furthermore, we've demonstrated that the space of refined unordered partitions is equivalent to the space of unordered configurations of points with an assigned order. We've also shown that when the set of points has fewer than three elements, the space of refined unordered partitions is equivalent to the space of unordered configurations of points with an assigned order, and we've established an isomorphism that relates the space of refined ordered partitions to the space of ordered configurations of points with an assigned order for certain types of refined orderings.

A recent advancement in medical brain lesion synthesis, known as the Adversarial Variational Recurrent Neural Network (AV-RNN), has been building upon the foundation of Markov Random Field-based models. However, these models are limited by their reliance on manually predefined parameters, which can result in suboptimal generated lesions. To address this, a more flexible approach is needed that can learn both a generative model and a set of implicit rules governing lesion formation. Towards this goal, a new method is proposed, which incorporates a learned graph-structured neural network into a Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) framework. The proposed method utilizes a Progressive Neural Network (ProgressNet) that is trained through both an adversarial system and a repeated graph-structured neural network, ultimately producing a more accurate set of realistic brain lesions. Experimental results show that this method surpasses state-of-the-art techniques in terms of naturalness and size accuracy of generated lesions. Moreover, the proposed method exhibits greater flexibility in modeling complex lesion formations, leading to enhanced learning capabilities and greater generalizability.

A set of quantum states is considered unextendable if its combination does not surpass a certain point, yet cannot be described through a loaly-independent quantum source. Research has shown that unextendable product bases (UPBs) exhibit quantum nonlocality, exhibiting behavior that cannot be explained by local operations and measurement alone. Our study investigates the robust quantum nonlocality of UPBs in various systems, including continuous variables, symmetric systems, and systems with multiple forms of entanglement. Using a novel approach, we demonstrate that a particular UPB exhibits robust quantum nonlocality in all mentioned systems, meeting certain criteria. Furthermore, we propose a scenario for continuously variable UPBs that may indicate robust quantum nonlocality, despite not meeting the required criteria. UPBs with diverse sizes and ranks also display robust quantum nonlocality, as proven through both theoretical and practical means. Our study provides the first comprehensive look at the robust quantum nonlocality of UPBs in diverse systems and offers opportunities for experimental verification.

The coordination of automated telescopes in large surveys poses an interesting problem at the intersection of astronomy and applied cryptography. The slow update time of these systems makes real-time cryptographic challenges necessary, limiting the scope of applicable secure coordinate protocols. We evaluate the performance of a previously proposed protocol, designed to ensure the secure and private sharing of telescope coordinates for the SDSS-V, and find it infeasible due to slow communication times. A key factor in this issue is the limited scope of practical challenge-response protocols, which restricts the protocol's usability in such applications. We discuss the implications of these findings for large-scale astronomical surveys that share telescope data.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for efficient program analysis and verification, leveraging graph transformations and matching. However, efficiently developing GP 2 programs poses difficulties for programmers who are not experts in graph theory, due to the required explicit handling of graph structures. To overcome these challenges, we enhanced the GP 2 compiler with node ordering optimization, reducing graph traversal inefficiencies and making-programmer tasks more manageable. Additionally, we incorporated a wrapper facility that bypasses explicit graph handling, allowing for the inclusion of inner nodes in graph matches. These innovations were demonstrated through a program analysis example for fixed-point calculations.

A task-agnostic attribute extraction framework is proposed that leverages contrastive learning for both supervised and unsupervised attribute learning. The proposed framework is comprised of three primary modules. Firstly, a contrastive learning module uses the Isolation Transformation (ISOLATION-TC) operator to isolate within each class while pushing away attribute values from other classes. Secondly, a bridge construction module integrates unsupervised attribute extraction using the K-Means ISOLATION-TC (KIS) algorithm, correlating unsupervised and supervised attribute learning. Thirdly, a refinement module is introduced to avert attribute value misclassification and rectify incongruities between the attribute code and discrete values. The proposed framework is experimentally evaluated on diverse datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and generality in attribute extraction.

We've developed a novel infinite set of star normal quotient networks known as the twisted wreath type. This set expands on previous constructions involving generalized Cartan graphs and harmonic Cartan graphs. Our infinite set also includes Cartan graphs and the solvable minimal finite quotient network, sol, which was unknown prior to this discovery. Additionally, we've established that the twisted wreath type networks have root systems and can be represented in Euclidean space, making them subgraphs of a finite solvable group of Ash.

Working with categorical data for predictive modeling is challenging due to its exponential complexity. Despite this difficulty, many features in real-world datasets consist of categorical variables. The complexity of these variables can be managed by representing them as a small number of discrete factors, with a dimensionality that is much smaller than the total number of categories. The Enhanced Group Lasso model is a novel method that is designed to handle such data by limiting the number of active factors across all categorical variables. In contrast to traditional Group Lasso approaches, this model encourages a smaller number of factors to be shared across variables, with an alternative that involves a smaller number of factors being selected from each variable individually. The Enhanced Group Lasso model can be solved using an efficient and feasible algorithm, with an analysis that provides a theoretical bound on its performance. The results of experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of the Enhanced Group Lasso model when compared to state-of-the-art methods, with a particular advantage in terms of predictive performance.

Recent advances in large language models have shown tremendous potential, delivering outstanding performance in various tasks such as text generation, question-answering, and summarization. Despite these achievements, the community remains unaware of the underlying knowledge these models possess, as their internal workings are not fully transparent. A key challenge lies in the disordered nature of the embedded knowledge, which encompasses tens of billions of parameters and is derived from an unordered corpus of text. Because of this, traditional methods of studying this knowledge, such as through relation paths in pre-trained models, have been found wanting. This paper introduces a novel approach, structured insight infusion (SKIILL), which enables the examination of complex knowledge within large language models by verifying the coherence of pre-generated text samples. Our evaluation shows that this method is more effective than existing approaches and highlights the significance of considering order in the analysis of ordered relations. Furthermore, SKIILL reveals crucial insights into the knowledge embedded within these models, which we distill into key findings.

This article explores the properties of a family of nonlocal diffusion models, which are based on space-time fractional in time (STFT) derivatives. We express these STFT operators as a combination of local and fractional components, confirming their well-posedness in appropriate L^p spaces. The article also examines the fractional limit case, which yields a relevant model, as well as the local limit case, which corresponds to a classic heat model. The article further investigates the existence and non-existence coefficients for positive solutions, obtaining results for the Laplace operator and bounded domain cases. The article also discusses Dirichlet problem existence and uniqueness results for the STFT operator, while addressing potential issues of weak singularity and space-time fractional elasticity problem existence. The article further provides a variational structure for the STFT operator, while discussing its link to fractional peristalsis models. The article further explores nonlocal elasticity and peristalsis models, while discussing their implications and future research directions.

When creating panoramic images, individuals generally prefer their viewpoint to be oriented downwards, which is influenced by an innate human preference for downward gaze. This study is the first to investigate how users' parallax control preferences are affected by the direction of their gaze in panoramic stitching. Our findings indicate that users are more comfortable controlling the parallax when their gaze is downward, and this level of comfort drops significantly when their gaze is directed either at a neutral angle or upwards. Based on these findings, two user-friendly methods for parallax control were developed, which can be easily integrated into automated stitching algorithms to improve their usability. Our research also implies that the ease of parallax control may depend on the user's level of discomfort with the direction of their gaze, and we believe this aspect deserves further investigation in the context of user experience.

The Eisenstein series for $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ have a combinatorial property as their zeros are influenced by the combinations of certain values originating from the zeros of Eisenstein series for $GL(k,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ and $GL(l,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$. This combinatorial aspect can be expressed through a set of rules that determine how the zeros of the Eisenstein series for $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ are generated from the zeros of the Eisenstein series for $GL(k,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ and $GL(l,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$. These rules can be represented by a sequence of combinatorial actions that include the intersection of certain cones, modifications of the weights, and rearrangements of the factors. Furthermore, the combinatorial property of the Eisenstein series for $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ implies that the zeros of the Eisenstein series for $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ are entirely described by the zeros of the Eisenstein series for $GL(k,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ and $GL(l,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$, resulting in

Our research involves developing a cutting-edge biophysical computational model of the brain, specifically focusing on a region critical to movement control that is adversely affected in Parkinson's disease patients. The model is designed for marmoset monkeys, one of the primary species used in Parkinson's research with advanced brain scanning technology. Although studies on human brains have significant implications, there's a need to translate findings into non-human primates due to ethical considerations. However, existing computational models for Parkinson's disease primarily apply to human brains, necessitating the creation of a new model tailored to marmoset monkeys. This project leverages extensive electroencephalography data from marmoset monkeys obtained during different sleep stages to inform the development of a highly detailed brain simulations environment. The model's structure is an accurate representation of a marmoset monkey's brain and incorporates more than 10 different neurotransmitters that play crucial roles in regulating the brain's electrical activity. It also accounts for the unique scalp-to-brain dimensions of marmoset monkeys, eliminating any size-related discrepancies. Furthermore, our approach enables the simulation of brain activity over an extended period, exceeding 100 seconds, which is essential for modeling the disease's progression. The fully functional model will be available online for researchers to explore and is an important step towards using computational models to investigate the underlying causes of Parkinson's disease in marmoset monkeys.

The project aims to enhance the aesthetic appeal of line vector maps used in various applications, such as web browsers and geographic information systems, by applying sophisticated anti-aliasing techniques originally designed for raster graphics. A key challenge lies in maintaining optimal performance for large-scale maps without compromising user interaction. To achieve this, we developed a customized algorithm that leverages GPU processing to render high-quality lines at interactive speeds. The development of this technique involved modifying the line rendering pipeline and exploring novel strategies for combining anti-aliasing filters. Our algorithm demonstrates notable improvements over traditional methods, delivering more engaging and visually appealing line vector maps.

Our team used the KOOLS-IFU on Seimei Telescope to gather data on 9 ultra/luminous infrared galaxies with distances from us of less than 160 million light years. We extracted information about gas velocities and distributions in these galaxies, and through spectral analysis, identified several molecular gas species including hydrogen and various metal ions, likely to have originated from the galactic environment. Our results show that hydrogen velocity in these galaxies ranges from 1200 to 2500 km/s, and in some cases, we observed velocity differences of more than 1000 km/s within a single galaxy, indicating potential for gas instability and star formation. Further analysis of oxygen emission, however, revealed a deficit of oxygen in some galaxies, which could be attributed to the recycling of oxygen back into later stages of stellar evolution, as well as the need for more extensive data.

A new class of transcendental radial basis function (RBF) interpolation formulas is presented, resulting in a novel form-conserving quasi-interpolation operator for multivariate functions. The new RBF formula is a modified form of the Bell manifold function, and its characteristics, including positive definiteness and monotonicity, are analyzed. A form-conserving quasi-interpolation operator is then constructed using this new RBF formula, and its order of convergence is proven to be O(h^2), where h represents the interpolation step size. The proposed operator is capable of handling any smooth function and maintains the original monotonicity and positive definiteness properties. Numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the operator's effectiveness.

Weather conditions are complicated and affect various aspects of daily life, especially for road navigation. Generally, road surfaces are classified into different types, such as highways, urban roads, and gravel roads, each prone to distinct weather conditions. A recent trend in utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for weather classification has emerged, but these methods are limited by the small size of currently available datasets, which hinders their potential for real-world applications. To address this challenge, we present a large-scale dataset called ClimateCategorization, comprising over 25,000 images across five distinct climate classes. Furthermore, we introduce an innovative data enhancement technique called Inverse Data Completion, which leverages a regression head to focus on missing data and achieves notable improvements in dataset performance. When applied to the ClimateCategorization dataset, IDC yields outstanding results, reaching a mAP of 32.34% without augmentation, which significantly surpasses state-of-the-art methods not utilizing augmentation. When integrated with aggressive augmentation, the method exhibits a remarkable 42.75% mAP.

To improve speech separation, a Dual-Path Convolutional Recurrent Network (DPCRN) model is proposed that extracts two types of information from T-F units: global information and local information. The proposed DPCRN model adds two dual-path networks to a conventional Bi-directional RNN (BIDNN) framework. The dual-path networks are designed to capture these two kinds of information, and then two reduced representations are injected into the BIDNN. Experimental results show that the proposed DPCRN model leads to a notable gain of 0.319 in average mean opinion score (MOS) compared to the baseline BIDNN model, and outperforms all baseline models including a non-local RNN (NLBIDNN) model.

We examined how neutrino masses and an $f(R)$ gravity impact were affecting the rotation curves of galaxies in Model B of Malacrino and Mulchaiov (2015), which includes a range of neutrino masses up to 0.5 eV and a Model B $f(R)$ parameter value of -1.1x10^-5 at a comoving scale of 10^17 cm. 

By applying a response surface design, we determined how a 1 eV increase in neutrino mass and a one-order-of-magnitude increase in the impact of $f(R)$ gravity on the Hubble constant at a comoving scale of 10^17 cm respectively affect the turn-around radii of dark matter structures in Model B. 

We discovered that a 1 eV increase in neutrino mass results in a 50% increase in the turn-around radii of galaxy-like systems, while the same-scale impact of $f(R)$ gravity on the Hubble constant at a comoving scale of 10^17 cm causes the turn-around radii of these systems to be 30% larger. 

However, we found that the influence of $f(R)$ gravity on the Hubble constant at a comoving scale of 10^17 cm is significantly more pronounced than the effect of a 1 eV increase in neutrino mass.

Recently introduced multi-fluid models propose a novel approach to studying atmospheric circulation by dividing the atmosphere into distinct convective layers, each represented by a separate fluid. While this methodology simulates convective activity within each layer, it assumes that fluids do not mix. To evaluate the efficacy of this model, we developed a two-fluid model consisting of a warm, less dense fluid with reduced viscosity and a cooler, more dense fluid with normal viscosity properties, separated by horizontal boundaries. We conducted a series of experiments using this model and compared its outcomes to traditional single-fluid simulations of Rayleigh-Benard convection. Despite exhibiting similar patterns of circulation and heat transfer, the two-fluid simulations yielded enhanced Nusselt numbers at moderate Rayleigh numbers. However, the advantage of the two-fluid model diminished as Rayleigh numbers increased. Nusselt number was found to correlate with the flux of heavy fluid within the light fluid layer; this correlation held constant across both model types for the tested Rayleigh number ranges. Nusselt number was also found to switch from power-law behavior to a more complex relationship with Rayleigh number as the latter increased beyond a certain point. We attribute this change to the onset of turbulent circulation during certain Benard regime transitions. Nusselt number was observed to vary based on the heavy fluid flux within the light fluid layer; this variation became more pronounced as Rayleigh numbers increased, occurring before the transition to turbulent circulation. We investigate three aspects of entangling uncorrelated two-level atoms using their connection to Jaynes-Cummings systems. We demonstrate how varying the parameter of a beam splitter interaction can create different types of entanglement in both stationary and moving Jaynes-Cummings systems. We also examine the impact of different types of Jaynes-Cummings interactions on a single wire and find that certain types can lead to the creation of steady-state entanglement between unconnected atoms. Additionally, we find that in some cases, even small changes in a parameter can result in significant increases in entanglement.

The Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) is one of the primary detectors in the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, tracking particle interactions resulting from high-energy collisions. As part of the CMS upgrade, a new silicon pixel detector is being developed to enhance precision in the reconstruction of particle trajectories. The Phase-1 pixel detector prototype, comprising 608 slices with a novel readout chip design, was tested in 2013 with a beam of protons. Although initial analysis focused on the prototype's overall performance, a detailed investigation of the track reconstruction was conducted in the beam test, utilizing a larger dataset than before. With an increased number of hits available per track, studies were undertaken on the hit pattern used for the time-consuming global track fit. As a result, a new approach was developed to validate the track reconstruction coherence based on the hit pattern, leading to improved finding rate and efficiency. The study demonstrated that a hit pattern with a high number of hits per track (around 28) significantly improved the finding rate. Furthermore, a new method was proposed to predict the hit pattern along with findings on the track reconstruction in the presence of magnetic field.

A novel method using Kall\'en-Lehmann spectral decomposition has been successfully applied to compute the mass spectrum of the SU(2) glueball on the lattice, yielding a stable and oscillatory pattern of modes around the mass eigenvalue. The spectral density at the mass eigenvalue displays a sharp spike, characteristic of a discrete mode, and the amplitude of this spike is found to be invariant under the renormalization group, confirming the physical nature of this mode. The predicted mass eigenvalue of approximately 1.66 GeV is consistent with the outcomes of previous lattice simulations.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, understanding the underlying emotions of a micro-blog post has become a highly
desirable application in the field of emotional analysis. To attain this, several machine
learning models can be used, including but not limited to, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and
Multilayer Perceptron, among others. Given the time-sensitive nature of Twitter's dynamic
environment, it's essential to use a method that quickly delivers accurate results. A recent
approach involving the use of Long Short-Term Memory networks was tested on two datasets,
namely, Sentiment140 and SentiWordNet, with positive outcomes. However, when tested on the
Kaggle dataset, the model was found to have some limitations, specifically a high degree of
overfitting that resulted in inferior performance. To mitigate this, several enhancements
were made to the basic LSTM model, including multiple feature extraction techniques and
the addition of dropout and batch normalization, which ultimately yielded a more
efficient model with reduced overfitting and better accuracy. The paper's proposed LSTM
model achieved a notable improvement in accuracy of around 45% on the Kaggle dataset,
which previously posed significant challenges due to its large size and complex nature.

A nonlinear interaction between an external massless field and a black hole can result in a more complex metric that may indicate a non-hydrodynamical behavior in the black hole's vicinity. We examine the interaction of a linear gravitational wave with a charged AdS black hole in this context, and through an approximation where the metric is slightly deformed, we derive the interaction's impact on the black hole's temperature, entropy, and energy. We find that the linear wave generates a thermodynamic response in the black hole's shadow, and the entropy and energy exhibit nonlinear changes that correspond to an increase in the black hole's capacity.

We investigate the connection between quantum entanglement and classical correlation in continuous-variable systems by examining the Wigner function's correlation, which serves as a measure for both phenomena. By applying this approach to optical systems and Gaussian states, we demonstrate that the proposed measure yields a clear indication of both quantum entanglement and correlation. Furthermore, we show that our correlation measure is essentially a derivative of the Fock-space Husimi function's correlation, which is directly related to the tomographic depth of an optical state. Consequently, we can utilize our correlation measure to identify the onset of synchronization in optical states by analyzing the tomographic depth of their Wigner functions.

Conversational interfaces are increasingly being used in various settings, such as customer service platforms, where the number of potential responses is limited, but in other situations, like open-domain conversations, the potential answers are virtually endless. Achieving high quality and user engagement in these conversations becomes a challenging problem to tackle. In this paper, we introduce a role-defined conversation framework that can handle open-domain conversations by assigning specific roles to both the human and machine participants, with the machine acting as a director to guide the conversation. To populate the director's response set, we propose a multi-task, multi-role framework that can handle the generation of not only pre-defined response roles but also new, unseen roles, using a combination of role-based and sentence-level classification to determine the director's response. We further introduce the Role Defined Conversation Data (RDCData), a large-scale conversation dataset that includes director response data, and evaluate our proposed director response data generation framework on this dataset, with results showing significant improvements over existing baselines. Human evaluation of our framework's conversations also show high quality ratings, with many conversations being natural and engaging.

As the number of pests affecting agriculture continues to rise, so does the usage of pesticides, which not only harms humans but also contaminates plants and affects biodiversity.  A powerful mathematical approach called Applied Combinatorial Optimization (ACO) has shown significant promise in addressing complex challenges such as optimizing pest control, though it has seen limited adoption within the scientific community associated with plant pathology.  In our research, we transformed the problem of managing fungal diseases in strawberries into an ACO-compatible challenge, successfully leveraging this method to reduce the application of fungicides by 20% and discover a previously unknown treatment schedule, ultimately resulting in a 10% decrease in disease occurrence.  Our findings highlight the potential for ACO to address key issues in plant pathology and we believe our approach can be readily adapted to address similar problems in other fields.

As 360-degree virtual travel videos gain popularity, predicting viewer subtitles becomes increasingly important for providing personalized information. Viewport forecasts represent a natural extension of this challenge, as they suggest specific views to viewers. Current approaches to viewport prediction are largely driven by data about viewer behavior, but a novel subtitle-driven framework is proposed that utilizes subtitles to forecast viewer views. The proposed framework consists of three modules: a data preprocessing step that combines subtitles with 3D spatial information from the video, features are then extracted using techniques like word2vec and CNN, and a subtitle-driven model is used to predict viewer views based on these features. The proposed framework is evaluated against a state-of-the-art baseline model using a dataset specifically created for subtitle-driven viewport prediction, and it achieves a 24.5% increase in accuracy. The findings of this study are validated through user feedback, and a comparison is made with an alternative approach that combines subtitle-driven and behavior-driven forecasting.

Tensor network methods have successfully modeled diverse conditions, including thermal states and time-dependent situations, despite not being naturally precise at interfaces between different regions. This issue arises because approximations are made during the implementation of these models, leading to a loss of accuracy at these interfaces. In contrast, our new approach focuses on achieving localized errors when representing thermal and time-dependent phenomena with tensor networks. In the case of equilibrated thermal states, this means drawing from a set of cross-correlations that characterize the thermal state, and for time-dependent situations, this involves integrating the time evolution over a period to maintain precision. We demonstrate the benefits of this approach by applying it to the finite temperature spin-1/2 Heisenberg chain and the Dirac equation, showing that local errors lead to a more gradual decline in performance than traditional tensor network methods.

We develop a decoupling theory for a limited class of expressions within the Hardest Problem Solver (HPS) framework, a symbolic algebra system used for solving dynamic mathematical problems. By understanding how HPS expressions are minimized, we can prevent overestimation or conservativeness in its numerical solution method. To this end, we create a new concept called "restricted effectiveness" to identify potentially minimizing HPS expressions. However, the complexity of HPS expressions hinders direct analysis, so we employ a reachability analysis to indirectly assess their minimization potential. We then propose a new, more efficient decoupling strategy that leverages both the complexity of HPS expressions and the results of the reachability analysis. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy on a set of benchmark problems, showing that it yields more accurate and conservative estimates compared to the existing HPS method.

In this research, we establish a nonisotropic $p$-capacity inequality that mirrors the isoperimetric inequality. As a result, we derive a nonisotropic Minkowski inequality. Our proof of the nonisotropic $p$-capacity inequality involves exploiting a modification of the wheel inequality and an elementary analysis of the nonisotropic $L^p$ norm.

The Microscope space mission aims to test the equivalence principle with an unprecedented level of precision. To achieve this goal, researchers must first remove non-lab-based noise from the data. The most prominent obstacle in this effort is the elimination of glitches, which are sudden, brief electrical anomalies likely caused by cosmic rays. These events are difficult to distinguish from potential violations of the equivalence principle due to their similar duration and amplitude. The statistics of glitches were studied using data from the LISA PathFinder test masses at 0.1 Hz to 0.003 Hz and found to vary in frequency, with rates peaking at 0.015 Hz. A simple model was developed to simulate glitches and their impact on equivalence principle testing. The estimated impact on test results shows that glitches could significantly affect the mission's outcome, perhaps even determining whether a particular path is compatible with the equivalence principle.

X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy was utilized to create precise nanoscale gradients of surface energy and hydrophobicity on silicon wafer surfaces. We observed the dynamic behavior of colloidal particles at various distances from a steady hydrophobic-surface contact line. By modifying surface energy and hydrophobicity, different types of particles were attracted to either the air-liquid interface or the solid-liquid interface. We found that particles near the air-liquid interface can be repelled by surface tension forces. Analytically modeling this interaction, we identified two regimes: in the thin-film regime, particles are influenced by the curved surface of Pascal's spheres, while in the large-distance regime, particles are affected by the meniscus's curvature. Conversely, in the presence of an attractive force between the particle and the surface, we model the particle's movement along the surface using a Langevin dynamics simulation. We discovered that even when the particle is drawn into an imperilized state, it can still be driven by thermal energy, resulting in oscillatory motion between the surface and the air-liquid interface.

The minimum strong shortest path cover with k-hops in a graph G is the smallest number of sets needed among all k-hops strong shortest path covers, where we also examine 2-hops covers for specific graphs and show the general k-hops cover problem is NP-complete.

The impact of infrared renormalons in the color dipole gluon distribution's variance is being quantified, and calculations demonstrate how non-linear small-x saturation impacts shift the Borel plane's initial IR pole from $2/\beta_2$ to $1/\beta_2$, thereby changing the estimated uncertainty to approximately $\chi^2$/df = 1 for the CERN LHCb collabration's TMD PDF measurements taken between kinematic ranges $0.01<x<0.1$ and $0.01<y<0.1$.

This study examines the amphibian model, a process influencing the survival of endangered species that has been released into the wild. We are specifically exploring the amphibian model on a branching process, where the model is run through an infinite number of generations. Our analysis focuses on determining the critical density for the model's extinction-minimum support criterion. Unlike other models, the amphibian model's critical density is not a measure of the probability of survival but rather a measure of the size of the environment.
